pages.targetText: Dạ, cho tôi một phần bún chả.
pages.englishText: One portion of bun cha, please.
pages.canonicalTargetText: Dạ, cho tôi một phần bún chả.
pages.pronunciation: yah cho toy mot fun boon cha
pages.context: Use this after the restaurant name is understood and you are ready to order one serving of bun cha.

chunks.vietnamese: Dạ, cho tôi một phần bún chả.
chunks.english: One portion of bun cha, please

pages.atGlance: This is the restaurant action phrase for ordering at Bún chả Hương Liên. It turns name recognition into a real order a beginner can say.
pages.quickSay: Say the whole line once while pointing at the menu or photo. Dạ keeps it soft, and một phần keeps the order simple.
pages.breakdownBody: The useful frame is cho tôi plus a quantity and dish name. Swap the dish later, but keep the polite opener for walk-in restaurant moments.
pages.useItWith: Use it after the host, server, or counter already knows where you are sitting or what menu you are pointing at.
pages.whenToUse: Use this at a table, counter, or food stall when the next task is ordering one serving, not asking about the restaurant itself.
pages.goodToKnow: Portion words matter more than long explanations. If you need two, point to the number or use the two-ticket/two-item pattern from nearby pages.
pages.exploreNextBody: Go next to drink, bill, taxi, or recommendation phrases that complete the restaurant visit.
pages.rationale: Required by EP-001 as a live restaurant interaction row. It is a full canonical phrase page because the row is visible and playable in future imports.

pages.targetText: Cho tôi trà đá.
pages.englishText: Iced tea, please.
pages.canonicalTargetText: Cho tôi trà đá.
pages.pronunciation: cho toy cha da
pages.context: Use this after the server knows you are ordering and the drink is the next small item.
pages.atGlance: Cho tôi trà đá is the short table line after the main dish is understood. It keeps the drink request easy at a casual restaurant.
pages.quickSay: Say it while pointing to the drink list or glass. Cho tôi keeps the request direct without turning it into a long sentence.
pages.breakdownBody: Cho tôi is the useful ordering frame. Trà đá is iced tea, a common cold-table drink in casual restaurant moments.
pages.useItWith: Use it after ordering food, asking what is available, or answering a server who is waiting for the drink choice.
pages.whenToUse: Use it at a table, food stall, or casual counter when the drink order is the only thing left to say.
pages.goodToKnow: If the server says hết rồi, the item is out. Point to another drink or use a recommendation phrase next.
pages.exploreNextBody: Go next to the longer iced-tea phrase, bill, taxi, or recommendation pages.
pages.rationale: Required by EP-001 because the pilot visible row says Cho tôi trà đá, not the longer existing one-iced-tea page.

pages.targetText: Gọi giúp tôi taxi được không?
pages.englishText: Can you call me a taxi?
pages.canonicalTargetText: Gọi giúp tôi taxi được không?
pages.pronunciation: goy zoop toy tak see duoc khong
pages.context: Use this at a restaurant, attraction, hotel desk, or shop when you need help getting a taxi back.

chunks.vietnamese: Gọi giúp tôi taxi được không?
chunks.english: Can you call me a taxi?

pages.atGlance: This is the simple ride-back phrase that many city and restaurant pages need. It asks for the action directly without explaining the whole travel problem.
pages.quickSay: Say it while showing your destination or hotel address. The other person can then call, point to a pickup spot, or suggest a ride app.
pages.breakdownBody: The phrase is built from call, help me, taxi, and a soft question ending. Those pieces make it useful beyond one city page.
pages.useItWith: Show the hotel card, map pin, booking screen, or address right after you say it so the ride request has a clear destination.
pages.whenToUse: Use it after a meal, attraction visit, market stop, or hotel desk conversation when leaving is the next task.
pages.goodToKnow: Taxi is widely understood, but the destination still needs to be visible. Keep the phrase short and let the helper choose the easiest way to call.
pages.exploreNextBody: Go next to pickup, stop, payment, and address-check phrases for the rest of the ride.
pages.rationale: Required by multiple deferred place and restaurant rows as a visible linked phrase for leaving a real location.

pages.targetText: Dạ, cho tôi một tô phở.
pages.englishText: One bowl of pho, please.
pages.canonicalTargetText: Dạ, cho tôi một tô phở.
pages.pronunciation: yah cho toy mot toh fuh
pages.context: Use this at a pho shop when you want the order to be one clear bowl, not a long menu discussion.
pages.youMayHear: Bò hay gà? / Tô lớn hay nhỏ?

chunks.vietnamese: Dạ, cho tôi một tô phở.

pages.atGlance: This gives the Phở Bát Đàn page a real order sentence after the restaurant name has done its job.
pages.quickSay: Say it while pointing at pho on the menu. If staff ask a follow-up, listen for beef, chicken, big, or small.
pages.breakdownBody: Một tô is the bowl-size frame. It pairs naturally with pho and other soup/noodle dishes.
pages.useItWith: After this phrase, the next useful question may be about size, beef/chicken, herbs, or payment.
pages.whenToUse: Use it at a pho counter or table when you already know what you want and need the order taken quickly.
pages.goodToKnow: Pho shops may ask short follow-up questions. Keep your phone or menu open and answer with pointing if the words come fast.
pages.exploreNextBody: Go next to recommendation, bill, drink, and drop-off phrases around the restaurant visit.
pages.rationale: Required by EP-002 as a full canonical support target for a named restaurant page.

pages.targetText: Có món nào nổi tiếng không?
pages.englishText: What is popular here?
pages.canonicalTargetText: Có món nào nổi tiếng không?
pages.pronunciation: koh mon nao noy tyeng khong
pages.context: Use this when the place is known for food but you want staff to point you toward an easy order.
pages.youMayHear: Món này. / Phở bò. / Bún chả.

chunks.vietnamese: Có món nào nổi tiếng không?

pages.atGlance: This asks for a recommendation without ranking any dish. It is useful when a menu is crowded and pointing is easier than reading.
pages.quickSay: Say it with the menu open. The answer will often be a dish name, a point, or a short suggestion.
pages.breakdownBody: Món nào asks which dish, while nổi tiếng asks for what is known or popular at that place.
pages.useItWith: Use this before ordering, then follow with one bowl, one portion, or a diet/allergy phrase if needed.
pages.whenToUse: Use it at restaurants, cafes, and food stalls when you want one practical suggestion instead of a full explanation.
pages.goodToKnow: This is a question, not a factual claim. It keeps the app durable because it lets staff answer for the current menu.
pages.exploreNextBody: Go next to order, ingredient, and bill phrases.
pages.rationale: Required by EP-002 to support a restaurant page with a menu/recommendation interaction.

pages.targetText: Cho tôi xuống ở đây được không?
pages.englishText: Can you drop me off here?
pages.canonicalTargetText: Cho tôi xuống ở đây được không?
pages.pronunciation: cho toy zoong uh day duoc khong
pages.context: Use this when the driver is close enough and you want to get out at the current spot.

chunks.vietnamese: Cho tôi xuống ở đây được không?
chunks.english: Can you drop me off here?

pages.atGlance: This is a ride-ending phrase for streets, restaurants, and landmarks. It is softer than a command and useful when the exact entrance is unclear.
pages.quickSay: Say it when the car is near your stop. Point to the curb or map pin if the driver needs the exact place.
pages.breakdownBody: Xuống is the key ride word: getting out, getting off, or being let down at a stop.
pages.useItWith: Use it after a street name, landmark name, or restaurant name has already guided the ride.
pages.whenToUse: Use it as the final step of a taxi, car, or motorbike ride when you can see the place or it is safe to stop.
pages.goodToKnow: Short drop-off phrases are normal in rides. A calm tone plus pointing is usually clearer than adding more words.
pages.exploreNextBody: Go next to stop-here, cash, fare, and street-confirmation pages.
pages.rationale: Required by restaurant and street pages as an exact visible drop-off support page.

pages.targetText: Dạ, cho tôi một phần cao lầu.
pages.englishText: One portion of cao lau, please.
pages.canonicalTargetText: Dạ, cho tôi một phần cao lầu.
pages.pronunciation: yah cho toy mot fun cow low
pages.context: Use this in Hoi An when cao lau is the dish you want to order directly.

chunks.vietnamese: Dạ, cho tôi một phần cao lầu.
chunks.english: One portion of cao lau, please

pages.atGlance: This is the beginner order phrase that makes a cao lầu page actionable once the dish name is familiar.
pages.quickSay: Say it while pointing at cao lầu on the menu. The phrase is short enough for a first-time traveler to use at a stall or restaurant.
pages.breakdownBody: The order frame is the same as other dish pages: polite opener, give me, one portion, dish name.
pages.useItWith: Pair it with ingredient or diet questions when you need to understand what is in the bowl before eating.
pages.whenToUse: Use this when you have chosen cao lầu and the next task is ordering, not asking where to find it.
pages.goodToKnow: Keep the dish name intact. Do not translate it word for word; treat it as a food name to recognize and say clearly.
pages.exploreNextBody: Go next to ingredient, pork, and where-to-find cao lầu pages.
pages.rationale: Required by EP-003 as title-preserving support for a dish page whose proposed patch changes the canonical Vietnamese title.

pages.targetText: Món này có gì?
pages.englishText: What is in this dish?
pages.canonicalTargetText: Món này có gì?
pages.pronunciation: mon nay koh zee
pages.context: Use this while pointing to a dish when you need a simple ingredient answer before ordering.
pages.youMayHear: Có thịt heo. / Có bò. / Rau.
pages.atGlance: This is the compact ingredient question behind the dish model. It helps when the menu words are still unfamiliar.
pages.quickSay: Point to the dish and ask the short question. Listen for the first ingredient word, then use a diet or allergy phrase if needed.
pages.breakdownBody: Món này means this dish. Có gì asks what it has, which is enough to invite a simple ingredient answer.
pages.useItWith: Use it before ordering cao lầu, bún bò Huế, soups, sauces, or any unfamiliar dish.
pages.whenToUse: Use it when the dish looks good but you need to know meat, seafood, peanuts, spice, or herbs before committing.
pages.goodToKnow: The answer may be a list or a point on the menu. If it comes too fast, ask for a repeat or show the ingredient you cannot eat.
pages.exploreNextBody: Go next to pork, seafood, vegetarian, and not-too-spicy pages.
pages.rationale: Required by EP-003 and EP-004 as a reusable full canonical page for dish ingredient support.

pages.targetText: Ở đâu có cao lầu ngon?
pages.englishText: Where has good cao lau?
pages.canonicalTargetText: Ở đâu có cao lầu ngon?
pages.pronunciation: uh dow koh cow low ngon
pages.context: Use this in Hoi An when you want a local direction toward a place serving cao lau.
pages.youMayHear: Gần đây. / Chỗ kia. / Ở phố này.

chunks.vietnamese: Ở đâu có cao lầu ngon?

pages.atGlance: This phrase keeps the dish page local to Hoi An by asking someone nearby for a practical food pointer.
pages.quickSay: Ask it at a hotel desk, cafe, or shop when you want a simple recommendation or direction.
pages.breakdownBody: The frame ở đâu có asks where there is something. Ngon asks for a good-tasting option without claiming a ranking.
pages.useItWith: Use it before opening maps or when a local can point to a nearby street or stall.
pages.whenToUse: Use it when the dish is the goal and you are still choosing where to eat.
pages.goodToKnow: This asks for local help, not a verified ranking. If the answer is a place name, show your map and ask them to point.
pages.exploreNextBody: Go next to order, ingredient, and repeat/show-me pages.
pages.rationale: Required by EP-003 to keep the cao lầu dish page useful without changing its canonical identity.

pages.targetText: Dạ, cho tôi một tô bún bò Huế.
pages.englishText: One bowl of bun bo Hue, please.
pages.canonicalTargetText: Dạ, cho tôi một tô bún bò Huế.
pages.pronunciation: yah cho toy mot toh boon bo hway
pages.context: Use this in Hue or at a Central Vietnamese restaurant when bún bò Huế is the bowl you want.
pages.youMayHear: Cay không? / Tô lớn hay nhỏ?

chunks.vietnamese: Dạ, cho tôi một tô bún bò Huế.
chunks.english: One bowl of bun bo Hue, please

pages.atGlance: This is the direct ordering sentence that lets the Bún bò Huế page teach an actual meal moment.
pages.quickSay: Say it while pointing to the dish name or photo. Expect a short question about spice, size, or toppings.
pages.breakdownBody: Một tô is the bowl frame. Bún bò Huế stays together as the dish name.
pages.useItWith: Use it before spice, ingredient, or payment phrases when the order is almost clear.
pages.whenToUse: Use it at a restaurant or stall when you know you want bún bò Huế and need a short order line.
pages.goodToKnow: If spice is a concern, order first and then add Không cay quá nhé. as the next sentence.
pages.exploreNextBody: Go next to not-too-spicy, ingredient, and bill pages.
pages.rationale: Required by EP-004 as a dish order support page.

pages.targetText: Không cay quá nhé.
pages.englishText: Not too spicy, please.
pages.canonicalTargetText: Không cay quá nhé.
pages.pronunciation: khong kai kwa nyeh
pages.context: Use this right after ordering when you want the dish milder but still natural.
pages.atGlance: This is the short spice-control phrase for dish pages. It asks for milder food without making the order complicated.
pages.quickSay: Say it after the dish name. Smile or point to yourself if you need to show it is your preference.
pages.breakdownBody: Không cay quá is the useful core: not too spicy. Nhé makes the request sound softer.
pages.useItWith: Use it after ordering soups, noodles, seafood, or sauces when spice level matters.
pages.whenToUse: Use it before the food is made or served, especially with Central Vietnamese dishes that may arrive spicy.
pages.goodToKnow: This does not promise the dish will be mild. It gives staff a clear preference early enough to help.
pages.exploreNextBody: Go next to ingredient, allergy, and order-again pages.
pages.rationale: Required by EP-004 as a full canonical spice support page.

pages.targetText: Cáp treo ở đâu?
pages.englishText: Where is the cable car?
pages.canonicalTargetText: Cáp treo ở đâu?
pages.pronunciation: cap treo uh dow
pages.context: Use this at an attraction or transport desk when the next step is finding the cable car area.
pages.youMayHear: Bên kia. / Đi thẳng. / Tầng dưới.
pages.atGlance: This is a stable attraction-navigation phrase for attractions where cable car movement is part of the visitor journey.
pages.quickSay: Ask it while showing your ticket or map. The answer will likely be a point, floor, direction, or sign.
pages.breakdownBody: Cáp treo is the important recognition chunk. Ở đâu turns it into a simple location question.
pages.useItWith: Use it after ticketing, at an entrance area, or whenever the route through the attraction is not obvious.
pages.whenToUse: Use it when you are already in the attraction flow and need the next place to stand or walk toward.
pages.goodToKnow: Keep the ticket, map, or phone visible. Attraction staff may answer with a gesture more than a full sentence.
pages.exploreNextBody: Go next to entrance, ticket, photo, and taxi-return phrases.
pages.rationale: Required by EP-005 and EP-013 as a stable sourced Ba Na Hills linked row.

pages.targetText: Bạn chụp giúp tôi được không?
pages.englishText: Can you take a photo for me?
pages.canonicalTargetText: Bạn chụp giúp tôi được không?
pages.pronunciation: ban choop zoop toy duoc khong
pages.context: Use this at a landmark when you want someone to take a photo with your phone.

chunks.vietnamese: Bạn chụp giúp tôi được không?
chunks.english: Can you take a photo for me?

pages.atGlance: This is the photo-help phrase that makes landmark pages interactive without turning them into guidebook descriptions.
pages.quickSay: Hold out your phone and ask the phrase. Smile and point to the spot if framing matters.
pages.breakdownBody: Chụp is the photo action, and giúp tôi makes the request friendly and clear.
pages.useItWith: Use it at bridges, viewpoints, entrances, and food spots when a quick photo is part of the visit.
pages.whenToUse: Use it when the person is nearby and the ask is small. Keep your phone unlocked and camera ready.
pages.goodToKnow: The phrase is friendly, but the phone handoff should feel easy. Keep the ask short and thank them after.
pages.exploreNextBody: Go next to thank-you, landmark where, and ride-back phrases.
pages.rationale: Required by EP-005 and EP-006 as a full canonical photo support row.

pages.targetText: Tài xế chờ ở đâu?
pages.englishText: Where does the driver wait?
pages.canonicalTargetText: Tài xế chờ ở đâu?
pages.pronunciation: tai seh cho uh dow
pages.context: Use this at an attraction when your ride or driver will wait while you visit.
pages.youMayHear: Ở cổng. / Bãi xe. / Ngoài kia.
pages.atGlance: This supports attraction pages where the visit has an entrance and a return point. It avoids assuming any current pickup policy.
pages.quickSay: Ask it before you go inside or up stairs. The answer may be a gate, parking area, or pointed direction.
pages.breakdownBody: Tài xế is driver, chờ is wait, and ở đâu asks where. Together they solve the return-point problem.
pages.useItWith: Use it when the driver, guide, or hotel desk is coordinating the pickup point.
pages.whenToUse: Use it before attractions with entrances, stairs, caves, pagodas, or large grounds where the pickup point matters.
pages.goodToKnow: Do not rely on memory alone. Pin the location on your map or take a photo of the meeting point.
pages.exploreNextBody: Go next to entrance, return taxi, and time-to-return pages.
pages.rationale: Required by EP-007 as stable visitor-flow support for Marble Mountains without importing time-sensitive policy claims.

pages.targetText: Anh chờ tôi ở đây được không?
pages.englishText: Can you wait for me here?
pages.canonicalTargetText: Anh chờ tôi ở đây được không?
pages.pronunciation: anh cho toy uh day duoc khong
pages.context: Use this with a male driver, guide, or helper when you need a short wait at the same spot.

chunks.vietnamese: Anh chờ tôi ở đây được không?
chunks.english: Can you wait for me here?

pages.atGlance: This is the wait-here phrase needed for area-style places like Sơn Trà where exact stops and return plans matter.
pages.quickSay: Say it only when the wait is realistic and short. Add a time if the driver asks bao lâu, meaning how long.
pages.breakdownBody: Chờ tôi is wait for me. Ở đây anchors the wait to the current spot.
pages.useItWith: Use it after naming the place or stop, then confirm the return time if needed.
pages.whenToUse: Use it for a short photo stop, viewpoint, pagoda stop, or pickup plan where the same driver may stay nearby.
pages.goodToKnow: Anh fits a male or older male-presenting driver. If the driver is a woman or the relationship is unclear, keep the destination visible and use a shorter wait phrase instead.
pages.exploreNextBody: Go next to return-time, exact-stop, and show-me pages.
pages.rationale: Required by EP-008 as a full canonical support target for area-route handling.

pages.targetText: Mấy giờ quay lại?
pages.englishText: What time do we come back?
pages.canonicalTargetText: Mấy giờ quay lại?
pages.pronunciation: may zuh quay lie
searchAliases: what time do we come back
pages.context: Use this when a driver, guide, or group plan needs a clear return time.
pages.youMayHear: Ba giờ. / Một tiếng nữa. / Ở đây.

chunks.english: What time do we come back?

pages.atGlance: This phrase turns a place visit into a plan. It is useful when you need the return time, not a description of the place.
pages.quickSay: Ask it while pointing to the meeting point or showing the route. Listen for a time or number of hours.
pages.breakdownBody: Mấy giờ asks what time. Quay lại is return or come back.
pages.useItWith: Use it with wait-here, driver-wait, or pickup-point phrases.
pages.whenToUse: Use it for viewpoint stops, attraction visits, group tours, and driver waits where timing matters.
pages.goodToKnow: If the answer is fast, ask them to write the time or show it on your phone.
pages.exploreNextBody: Go next to wait-here, say-again, and show-on-map pages.
pages.rationale: Required by EP-008 as a return-flow support page.

pages.targetText: Cho tôi đến đường Bạch Đằng.
pages.englishText: Please take me to Bach Dang Street.
pages.canonicalTargetText: Cho tôi đến đường Bạch Đằng.
pages.pronunciation: cho toy den duong bach dang
searchAliases: take me to Bach Dang Street
pages.context: Use this with a driver when Bạch Đằng Street is the destination or the street near your stop.
pages.youMayHear: Đường Bạch Đằng? / Ở đoạn nào?

chunks.vietnamese: Cho tôi đến đường Bạch Đằng.
chunks.english: Please take me to Bach Dang Street

pages.atGlance: This is the full driver sentence for the Đường Bạch Đằng street-pronouncer page.
pages.quickSay: Say it slowly, then show the address or map pin. Street names are safer when seen and heard together.
pages.breakdownBody: Đường means street. Treat Bạch Đằng as a name to recognize, not a phrase to translate.
pages.useItWith: Use it after practicing the street name by itself.
pages.whenToUse: Use it in taxis, ride-hailing, hotel desk directions, or walking help when the street is the anchor.
pages.goodToKnow: If the driver asks which part, show the exact address or nearby landmark.
pages.exploreNextBody: Go next to confirm-street and drop-off pages.
pages.rationale: Required by EP-009 to make the street page driver-ready without changing the street-name page.

pages.targetText: Đây có phải đường Bạch Đằng không?
pages.englishText: Is this Bach Dang Street?
pages.canonicalTargetText: Đây có phải đường Bạch Đằng không?
pages.pronunciation: day koh phai duong bach dang khong
pages.context: Use this when you are near the street and need a quick yes/no confirmation.

chunks.vietnamese: Đây có phải đường Bạch Đằng không?

pages.atGlance: This is the street confirmation row for Bạch Đằng. It helps when signs, maps, or pronunciation do not quite line up.
pages.quickSay: Ask it while showing the map. The answer should be yes, no, or a point toward the right side.
pages.breakdownBody: Đây có phải...không? is a yes/no confirmation frame around the street name.
pages.useItWith: Use it after a driver drops you nearby or while walking between streets.
pages.whenToUse: Use it when the street name matters more than a full address.
pages.goodToKnow: A pointed answer is useful. Watch the gesture before asking a longer follow-up.
pages.exploreNextBody: Go next to driver sentence, drop-off, and wrong-place pages.
pages.rationale: Required by EP-009 as a full canonical street confirmation target.

pages.targetText: Cho tôi đến đường Nguyễn Văn Linh.
pages.englishText: Please take me to Nguyen Van Linh Street.
pages.canonicalTargetText: Cho tôi đến đường Nguyễn Văn Linh.
pages.pronunciation: cho toy den duong nguyen van linh
searchAliases: take me to Nguyen Van Linh Street
pages.context: Use this with a driver when Nguyễn Văn Linh Street is the address anchor.
pages.youMayHear: Đường Nguyễn Văn Linh? / Đoạn nào?

chunks.vietnamese: Cho tôi đến đường Nguyễn Văn Linh.
chunks.english: Please take me to Nguyen Van Linh Street

pages.atGlance: This is the driver-ready sentence for the Nguyễn Văn Linh street pages.
pages.quickSay: Say the phrase, then show the map or address. The street name is the part to say slowly.
pages.breakdownBody: The frame is take me to plus đường and the street name.
pages.useItWith: Use it after checking whether the street is near or confirming the name.
pages.whenToUse: Use it in taxis, ride apps, hotel desks, or walking directions where Nguyễn Văn Linh is the anchor.
pages.goodToKnow: Long names are easier when the driver sees the text. Use your pronunciation as a backup, not the only proof.
pages.exploreNextBody: Go next to confirmation, near-here, and show-me pages.
pages.rationale: Required by EP-010 and EP-016 as a street-pronouncer driver support page.

pages.targetText: Đây có phải đường Nguyễn Văn Linh không?
pages.englishText: Is this Nguyen Van Linh Street?
pages.canonicalTargetText: Đây có phải đường Nguyễn Văn Linh không?
pages.pronunciation: day koh phai duong nguyen van linh khong
searchAliases: is this Nguyen Van Linh Street
pages.context: Use this when you are near Nguyễn Văn Linh Street and need a yes/no check.

chunks.vietnamese: Đây có phải đường Nguyễn Văn Linh không?
chunks.english: Is this Nguyen Van Linh Street?

pages.atGlance: This confirms the street after a ride, walk, or map check. It is a yes/no phrase, not a request for a long route.
pages.quickSay: Ask while pointing to the street or map. Let the answer be a yes, no, or gesture.
pages.breakdownBody: Đây có phải...không? wraps the street name in a simple confirmation frame.
pages.useItWith: Use it before walking farther or when a driver stops near the street.
pages.whenToUse: Use it when the street name is visible but you are not fully sure it is the right one.
pages.goodToKnow: If the answer is no, switch to Hình như không đúng chỗ or ask them to show you.
pages.exploreNextBody: Go next to driver sentence, near-here, and wrong-place recovery.
pages.rationale: Required by EP-010 as a full street confirmation support page.

pages.targetText: Hình như không đúng chỗ.
pages.englishText: I think this is not the right place.
pages.canonicalTargetText: Hình như không đúng chỗ.
pages.pronunciation: hin nyu khong dung cho
pages.context: Use this gently when the stop, street, or address seems wrong and you need to reset the route.
pages.youMayHear: Để tôi xem. / Đúng mà. / Ở bên kia.

chunks.english: I think this is not the right place

pages.atGlance: This is a soft reset phrase for street and route pages. It avoids blame and keeps the conversation practical.
pages.quickSay: Say it calmly while showing the map or address. Then wait for the driver or helper to check.
